subject: history_social
passage: On the cliffs of the Azores, a chain of Portuguese islands in the mid-Atlantic, stand small whitewashed huts called vigias. For more than a century, men sat in them from dawn to dusk scanning the sea for the spout of a sperm whale, and when one was sighted they set off a rocket to summon the boats. Whaling ended in the islands in the 1980s, but the vigias were not ______. Today lookouts with binoculars still work from the same huts, radioing the position of whales to tour boats carrying visitors who have come to watch the animals rather than hunt them.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: "But" sets up a contrast with the end of whaling, and the next sentence says lookouts "still work from the same huts." So the huts were not given up when whaling stopped: they were not "abandoned."
explanation.A: Correct. The huts stayed in use after whaling ended, so they were not abandoned.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The huts are still used every day by lookouts, so they clearly are still needed.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This reverses the point: the huts were in fact given a new purpose, serving tour boats instead of whalers.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Nothing in the text is about whether the huts can be seen.
